recent_articles.title: The political economy of cash transfers
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** budgetary allocation for unconditional cash transfers (UCT) has increased significantly, reaching 0.9% of GDP in 2026.  While **Government of India** officials and researchers warn that this expansion will increase future debt burdens and crowd out productive investment, the practice persists due to political incentives. The rise of UCT is driven by voter-targeted cash transfers, which have become a popular strategy for election campaigns. This trend has led to increased competition among parties, with promises of cash transfers becoming a key electoral tool.  However, critics argue that poorly designed UCT schemes fail to create long-term productive assets and can negatively impact fiscal sustainability.

recent_articles.title: Creeping risk: The Hindu Editorial on industrial accidents and neglect of risks - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Boiler explosions**, like the recent incident in Sakti, Chhattisgarh, are often caused by a gradual build-up of issues such as overpressure and scaling.  These incidents share similarities with other industrial disasters in India, including the Visakhapatnam gas leak and the Neyveli blast, highlighting systemic failures in boiler safety regulations. The current regulatory framework, which focuses on fabrication standards rather than continuous monitoring, has been criticized for failing to adequately address transient thermal and pressure imbalances that can lead to explosions.  The lack of surprise government inspections and a focus on "ease of doing business" have contributed to these issues, as evidenced by the exploitation of contract labor and inadequate safety measures in some facilities.

Despite these concerns, an IOCL representative denied any plans for relocation.

recent_articles.title: Assam election verdict hinges on parties reading the tea leaves right - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Assam Assembly election campaign is being heavily influenced by the tea tribe community, which comprises almost 20% of voters.  **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress**, promised daily wages of ₹450 and Scheduled Tribe status for six communities, including tea tribes, while **Hemant Soren**, Jharkhand Chief Minister, campaigned for a candidate from the **Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM)**, highlighting the lack of ST status for these communities in Assam.  The BJP is promising land rights to over 3.5 lakh families and raising minimum wages to ₹500. The JMM's entry into the race has complicated matters for both major parties, but its impact on the tea tribe vote remains uncertain.

recent_articles.title: Mulapeta seaport works will be completed by end of this year: Minister - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Minister for Roads and Buildings and Infrastructure B.C. Janardhana Reddy** stated that the **government** aims to complete pending works at the Mulapeta seaport within a year, despite previous delays attributed to land acquisition issues.  The visit by **Mr. Reddy** and **Agriculture Minister K. Atchannaidu** addressed concerns raised by local residents and aimed to ensure smooth progress on the project's completion. The ministers emphasized the seaport's potential to boost economic activity in the Srikakulam district and facilitate cargo exports for neighboring states.

recent_articles.title: Congress petitions Election Commission to cancel Assam CM’s candidature over ‘undisclosed assets’ - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Himanta Biswa Sarma**, the Chief Minister of Assam, is facing a petition from the **Assam Congress** to cancel his candidacy for the upcoming Assembly election. The petition alleges that he failed to disclose his wife's alleged offshore assets in his affidavit, violating the Representation of the People Act, 1951. A delegation led by former Chhattisgarh Chief Minister **Bhupesh Baghel** submitted the complaint to the Assam Chief Electoral Officer.  Sarma denies the allegations.

recent_articles.title: Amit Jogi sentenced to life imprisonment in Jaggi murder case from 2003 - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Chhattisgarh High Court** sentenced Amit Jogi, son of former Chief Minister Ajit Jogi, to life imprisonment for the 2003 murder of businessman-politician Ramavatar Jaggi. The court overturned a previous acquittal, stating that evidence clearly showed Amit Jogi as the mastermind behind the conspiracy and holding the trial court's decision as illegal.  Amit Jogi has appealed the verdict to the **Supreme Court**.

recent_articles.title: Pinarayi slams Rahul for drawing equivalence between LDF and Hindutva forces in Chhattisgarh - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** of Kerala criticized **Rahul Gandhi**, the Leader of the Opposition in Parliament, for accusing the **LDF** of being aligned with the **BJP**.  **Mr. Vijayan** stated that **Mr. Gandhi's** accusations were "brazenly misleading" and stemmed from ignorance about the history of the law used to arrest the nuns in Chhattisgarh. He also criticized the Congress party for its inaction during protests demanding the release of the nuns, highlighting their complicity in past Hindu majoritarian attacks on Christians in the state.

recent_articles.title: ₹20.10 crore sanctioned for Nagoba temple and ₹200 crore for integrated school in Boath - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Indian government** has approved a ₹20.10 crore project to beautify and develop the historic Nagoba Temple in Adilabad district, aiming to enhance tourist amenities and generate livelihood opportunities for local tribal populations.  The project includes infrastructure development, road connectivity, and storm water drain construction. Additionally, **the government** sanctioned a ₹200 crore project for a Young India Integrated Residential School (YIIRS) complex in Boath constituency of Adilabad district to improve educational infrastructure for disadvantaged students.

recent_articles.title: Sajjala criticises Amaravati push, alleges financial burden on people - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **YSR Congress Party** State coordinator **Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy** criticized **Nara Chandrababu Naidu's** Amaravati capital project, alleging it is financially burdensome and lacks practicality.  He accused **Naidu** of comparing regions like playing cards and criticized the three capitals proposal by former Chief Minister **Jagan Mohan Reddy**. **Reddy** argued that the Amaravati project was driven by corruption and unsustainable borrowing, while defending the MaViGun model as a more sustainable approach to capital development. He called for a rethink in the government's approach and emphasized people-centric, financially viable development models.

recent_articles.title: Union Home Ministry revises classification of districts affected by left-wing extremism - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** has re-categorized the number of left-wing extremism (LWE) affected districts in India, replacing "most affected" with "LWE affected," "districts of concern," and "legacy and thrust districts." While the total number of LWE districts remains unchanged at 38, the classification now reflects shifts in the severity of violence reported. The MHA reviewed the categorization three days before Home Minister Amit Shah declared the country "Naxal-free" and sent the new list to state police chiefs.  The ministry emphasized that a number of interventions have led to an improvement in the LWE situation, and the revised categorization will help ensure resources are allocated effectively.

recent_articles.title: Census 2027 kicks off: How to do self-enumeration: step-by-step guide - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **India's** Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner will conduct the 2027 census, a massive administrative and statistical exercise that collects demographic data on the entire country. The self-enumeration facility allows citizens to provide their household information online before enumerators visit, offering flexibility in filling out the census schedule.  The dates for self-enumeration vary by state and union territory, with most starting in April 2026. Census data is expected to be published within 2027 due to the digital nature of the process.

recent_articles.title: NIA, ED bust Maoist extortion, money laundering rackets - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Investigation Agency (NIA)** and the **Enforcement Directorate (ED)** have been actively disrupting the financial networks of banned Maoist outfits. The NIA has investigated over 100 cases, seized assets worth more than ₹40 crore, and filed chargesheets against several high-ranking operatives. The ED has attached assets worth over ₹12 crore and filed prosecution complaints against individuals who extorted money from businessmen, contractors, and workers.  Both agencies have successfully disrupted the financial operations of various Maoist groups across different states, including those linked to splinter groups like **The People’s Liberation Front of India**.

recent_articles.title: Prayer meeting in private dwellings does not require prior nod: Chhattisgarh HC - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Chhattisgarh High Court** ruled that individuals do not need prior permission from authorities to hold religious prayers or meetings in their private dwellings, as long as they comply with existing laws. The court's decision came after a petition by two residents challenging police notices prohibiting Christian prayer meetings at their residence.  The court stated that no law restricts such gatherings and that authorities can take action if there is noise pollution or law and order issues. This ruling follows similar decisions from the **Allahabad High Court** earlier this year.

recent_articles.title: Bastar close to being considered Naxal-free, possibility of revival extremely remote: IGP - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Inspector General of Police (Bastar Range) P. Sundarraj** stated that **Bastar** is close to becoming Naxal-free, with the likelihood of a large-scale revival of the Maoist movement appearing extremely remote.  He attributed this progress to increased anti-Naxal operations since January 2024, resulting in the death of over 500 cadres and the neutralization or surrender of many others. The police officer also highlighted the gradual integration of previously inaccessible areas like Abujhmad into the governance framework. **Mr. Sundarraj** emphasized that a truly Naxal-free situation requires the elimination of armed squads, the end of intimidation, and the reintegration of remaining cadres into society.

recent_articles.title: Barring one, entire top leadership of Maoists wiped out, Amit Shah tells Lok Sabha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** announced that the **Communist Party of India (Maoists)** leadership has been largely dismantled, with only one member remaining.  He attributed this success to a shift in policy and strong political will following the 2014 election. The government has achieved significant progress against Maoist violence, including the surrender of over 4,800 cadres, arrests of 2,218 members, and the deaths of 706 Maoists.  **Mr. Shah** highlighted the use of technology like drone surveillance and phone tracking in this effort. The government aims to declare India Naxal-free by March 31, 2026.

recent_articles.title: DGP appeals to Maoists to surrender and join mainstream - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **B. Shivadhar Reddy**, **Telangana** Director General of Police, appealed to **CPI (Maoist)** leaders and cadres operating underground to abandon violence, surrender their weapons, and join the democratic mainstream. He highlighted that over 721 individuals have surrendered in the past two years due to police efforts, receiving benefits like financial assistance under the Comprehensive Rehabilitation Scheme.  **Reddy** urged those currently hiding to return to society and live peacefully with their families, emphasizing security, dignity, and livelihood support for those who surrender. This appeal comes as the Union government's deadline to eliminate Left Wing Extremism approaches on March 31, 2026.

recent_articles.title: NDA, Opposition spar in LS over efforts to free country of Maoism - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** and **NDA** members in the Lok Sabha criticized the previous **UPA** government for its handling of Maoism, accusing it of failing to contain the threat.  They highlighted significant reductions in the "red corridor" under the current administration and emphasized the success of policies like Operation Green Hunt and the creation of CoBRA. The Congress countered by pointing to efforts made during their tenure, including the establishment of the Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) and emphasizing a balanced approach that prioritized both security and welfare.  The debate highlighted contrasting approaches to combating Maoism between the two governments.

recent_articles.title: Maoist campaign saw continuity across regimes, sharper push recently: Former MHA official - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** and **BJP** governments, under both the **Home Minister Amit Shah** and former Prime Minister **Manmohan Singh**, have pursued a consistent approach to tackling the Maoist problem.  Former security adviser **K. Vijay Kumar**, who served in both administrations, highlights the gradual gains made between 2006-2009, culminating in a deadline set by **Shah** for eradicating Left Wing Extremism by March 31, 2026.  He also notes that former Home Minister **P. Chidambaram** provided funding and resources to counter Maoist activity, while **Ajit Doval**, as National Security Advisor, focused on training local youths in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.  Kumar emphasizes the improvement in training, equipment, and coordination over time, despite challenges such as allegations of human rights violations against security forces.

recent_articles.title: A sidetracked railway in Visakhapatnam - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Despite the **Railway Board**'s announcement of the new South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone in 2019, progress has been slow. The lack of a Gazette notification to officially establish the zone has stalled operations and raised concerns about the government's commitment.  The delay has led to accusations from BJP leaders that Visakhapatnam is being unfairly treated by the **East Coast Railway (ECoR)** while also hindering the development of the Waltair division, which is crucial for Andhra Pradesh's economic growth.

recent_articles.title: What is the Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Bill? | Explained - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Maharashtra** government passed the Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Bill, 2026, which aims to prohibit unlawful religious conversions. The bill mandates a 60-day notice period for conversion and requires police registration of complaints related to forced conversions.  Civil society organizations have expressed concerns about the bill's potential impact on personal liberty and its constitutionality.  The bill has been supported by **Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis**, who stated that it is necessary to address increasing cases of forcible religious conversions. The bill has also been criticized for potentially targeting minority communities and raising administrative concerns regarding the lack of a certification system for religions.

recent_articles.title: Maoist killed in Sukma; IG urges surrender before March 31 deadline - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **Maoist** identified as Muchaki Kailash, wanted for civilian killings and carrying a ₹5 lakh reward, was killed in an encounter with security forces in Chhattisgarh's Sukma district. The **Sukma District Reserve Guard (DRG)** team initiated the operation based on intelligence about Maoist presence.  The **Union Home Ministry** has set March 31 as the deadline to eliminate Maoist activities.

recent_articles.title: ‘A double-engine govt. will de-risk people from political conflicts that hurt their development’: Rajeev Chandrasekhar - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Rajeev Chandrasekhar**, the Bharatiya Janata Party's State president in Kerala, is leading the party's efforts to challenge the LDF-UDF duopoly. He faces a tough battle in Nemom, where he competes against incumbent MLA V. Sivankutty and former Congress MLA K.S. Sabarinadhan.  While the BJP saw gains in local body elections, its vote share remains lower than in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Chandrasekhar emphasizes his party's outreach to minority communities and addresses concerns about incidents of violence against religious minorities. He argues that the BJP is not solely responsible for such events but acknowledges the need for law enforcement.  He also highlights the contrasting perspectives on disaster relief funds, with the LDF criticizing the Centre while pointing to the BJP-led government's own achievements in areas like health and education.

recent_articles.title: Polavaram displaced families seek land along Odisha, Chhattisgarh borders - The Hindu
recent_articles.sentiment_target: Polavaram District Collector K. Dinesh Kumar
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Families** living in the Polavaram irrigation project area appealed to **Polavaram District Collector K. Dinesh Kumar** for land for the Land-to-Land component of the Resettlement and Rehabilitation (R&R) package, citing their need for cultivable land for survival and livelihood.  The families, who have already parted with their land for the project, requested fertile land in Soderupadu, Sunnam Mataka, and Boorguvada along the borders of Odisha and Chhattisgarh. **Mr. Dinesh Kumar** met with residents of A.G. Koderu village and listened to their concerns about access to safe drinking water, healthcare, and Forest Rights Act (FRA) pattas.

recent_articles.title: 78 mandals in Andhra Pradesh exceed 40°C - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Andhra Pradesh** experienced temperatures exceeding 40°C in at least 78 mandals, with Gudur recording the highest of 42.4°C on Sunday (March 29, 2026). The **Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA)** issued alerts for several districts due to heatwave conditions expected in 87 out of 671 mandals.  The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** predicts a drop in temperatures next week with light showers, thunderstorms, and lightning in Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema until April 5th. The IMD also attributes the high temperatures to two upper air cyclonic circulations. APSDMA Managing Director Prakhar Jain advised residents to avoid open areas during thunderstorms and lightning.

recent_articles.title: Closure of eateries: Migrant labourers return to their native States - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Migrant labourers** from various states, who had been employed in eateries and catering units across **Andhra Pradesh**, are returning to their home states due to a shortage of commercial gas cylinders. This shortage has forced many businesses to close, leaving thousands of workers jobless.  The situation has impacted industries such as fast food centers, biryani points, sweet stalls, and roadside eateries, with some owners having to reduce their menus or shut down entirely.

recent_articles.title: Mann Ki Baat: Chhattisgarh farmers’ water conservation efforts earn praise; Vishnu Deo Sai calls it proud moment - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chhattisgarh** Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai expressed pride in **Prime Minister Narendra Modi's** recognition of the "Aawa Pani Jhonki" water conservation model in Korea district during his "Mann Ki Baat" broadcast.  Mr. Sai highlighted that over 1,200 farmers have implemented this innovative approach to collect rainwater, significantly improving groundwater levels. The Chief Minister also emphasized the government's efforts to promote self-reliance in fisheries and encourage a healthy lifestyle for rural economic growth.

recent_articles.title: What did the Supreme Court rule on Scheduled Castes and religion? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Supreme Court ruled that a person cannot be considered a member of the Scheduled Caste (SC) if they profess a religion different from Hinduism, Sikhism, or Buddhism. The Court upheld this decision based on the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, which states that individuals who "profess" a religion other than these faiths are not SCs.  The Court emphasized that conversion to any faith not listed in the order results in immediate loss of SC status and associated benefits. The ruling also addressed the question of reconversion to Hinduism, Sikhism, or Buddhism, stating that claimants must provide strong evidence for "reconversion" including renunciation of their previous religion, complete assimilation into the original caste, and acceptance by the community.  The Court acknowledged the complexities surrounding conversion and its impact on Scheduled Tribe (ST) status, emphasizing that ST status is determined by tribal attributes rather than solely based on religious affiliation.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh Govt cracks down on LPG cylinder hoarding, 97 FIRs registered - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai** of Chhattisgarh chaired a meeting to address concerns about hoarding of cooking gas amidst the ongoing war in West Asia.  Raids were conducted at 335 locations, resulting in the seizure of 3,841 LPG cylinders and the registration of 97 FIRs for suspected hoarding. **Mr. Sai** issued directives for stringent action against hoarding or black marketing of essential commodities and mandated regular monitoring of stock and supply at all petrol pumps and gas agencies.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh High Court says signs, gestures are oral evidence, upholds conviction of man for raping disabled woman - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Chhattisgarh High Court** ruled that testimony through signs and gestures will be considered substantive oral evidence, overturning the conviction of a man for raping a deaf and mute woman. The court found that the trial court took appropriate measures to ensure the victim's testimony was understood, including using a plastic doll during questioning.  The **High Court** upheld the conviction and sentence, stating the victim demonstrated competency through gestures and communication aids.

recent_articles.title: Coal India to set up 8 new coking coal washeries spending ₹3,300 crore - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Coal India**, the state-owned miner, plans to invest ₹3,300 crores in building eight new coking coal washeries with a combined capacity of 21.5 million tonnes per year. The expansion will be undertaken by **Central Coalfields Ltd.** and **Bharat Coking Coal Ltd.**, aiming to improve domestic coking coal quality and reduce reliance on imports.  The miner also plans to modernize existing facilities, bringing the total washing capacity to 18.35 million tonnes annually. India currently relies heavily on imports for its coking coal needs, despite having substantial reserves.

recent_articles.title: Chhattisgarh IPS officer suspended following harassment allegations - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Ratan Lal Dangi**, an IPS officer from Chhattisgarh, was suspended on March 26, 2026 following a departmental inquiry into allegations of harassment by a junior colleague's wife. The **home department** cited his conduct as unbecoming and unethical, violating the All India Services (Conduct) Rules, 1968, and tarnishing the police's image. Dangi denied the allegations, claiming he was being blackmailed. He has been ordered to remain at the Police Headquarters in Nava Raipur during his suspension period.

recent_articles.title: NHRC issues notice to Chhattisgarh government over death of 285 inmates in different jails of State in four years - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)** issued a notice to the **Chhattisgarh government** following reports of 285 inmate deaths in state jails over the past four years. The commission cited media reports and overcrowding as contributing factors, prompting them to demand a detailed report within two weeks detailing data on overcrowding, vacant doctor positions, and the government's response to these issues.  The **NHRC** is concerned about potential violations of human rights.
